questions.stem: An 18-month-old child has irritability, poor appetite, tachypnea, and persistent tachycardia after a viral illness. Which additional finding would most increase concern for heart failure from myocarditis?
questions.rationale: Hepatomegaly is a high-yield sign of systemic venous congestion in pediatric heart failure.

option_explanations.A: Common after viral illness but nonspecific.
option_explanations.B: Correct. It adds a cardiac congestion clue.
option_explanations.D: May occur with viral illness but is nonspecific.

questions.board_pearl: In young children, examine the liver when unexplained tachycardia and tachypnea persist.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old has chest pain and elevated troponin after a viral illness. Which ECG pattern is compatible with myocarditis but is not specific enough to establish the diagnosis alone?

options.B: Delta wave with short PR interval
options.D: Fixed epsilon wave as the sole finding
options.E: Normal sinus rhythm with no abnormalities

questions.rationale: ST-T abnormalities are common in myocarditis but are nonspecific and require clinical correlation.

option_explanations.A: Correct. They support but do not prove myocardial inflammation.
option_explanations.C: Suggests atrial flutter and is not a typical stand-alone myocarditis marker.
option_explanations.D: Raises concern for arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy rather than routine myocarditis.
option_explanations.E: A normal ECG does not exclude myocarditis but does not support it either.

questions.board_pearl: ECG can be abnormal in myocarditis, but no single routine tracing pattern is diagnostic.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old child has fever, tachycardia, hypotension, elevated inflammatory markers, and depressed LV function. He also has conjunctival injection, rash, and recent SARS-CoV-2 infection several weeks earlier. Which diagnosis most appropriately broadens the differential beyond isolated viral myocarditis?
questions.rationale: Multisystem inflammation after recent SARS-CoV-2 infection with shock and myocardial dysfunction is compatible with MIS-C and should not be labeled automatically as isolated myocarditis.

option_explanations.A: Correct. The multisystem inflammatory phenotype is the key discriminator.
option_explanations.B: Does not explain shock and ventricular dysfunction.
option_explanations.C: Would not explain the inflammatory mucocutaneous syndrome.
option_explanations.D: Could cause abdominal symptoms but not this cardiac/mucocutaneous pattern.
option_explanations.E: Would cause acute respiratory/hemodynamic findings without this inflammatory syndrome.

questions.board_pearl: When myocardial dysfunction occurs within a multisystem inflammatory syndrome, diagnose the systemic process rather than reflexively calling it isolated myocarditis.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old with suspected myocarditis has tachycardia, dyspnea, pulmonary crackles, and moderate LV systolic dysfunction but normal blood pressure and preserved mentation. Which management principle is most appropriate?

options.A: Treat as uncomplicated dehydration with repeated boluses
options.B: Use supportive heart-failure care with close monitoring and avoid unnecessary volume loading
options.C: Encourage ambulation to assess exercise tolerance
options.E: Delay cardiac monitoring until MRI confirms the diagnosis

questions.rationale: Supportive acute heart-failure management and monitoring are appropriate while avoiding volume strategies that could worsen congestion.

option_explanations.A: Repeated boluses can worsen pulmonary edema.
option_explanations.B: Correct. Management follows the hemodynamic phenotype while diagnostic evaluation continues.
option_explanations.C: Exercise is inappropriate during active disease.
option_explanations.D: Fever resolution does not establish hemodynamic stability.
option_explanations.E: Monitoring should not wait for advanced imaging.

questions.board_pearl: Treat the physiology you see; diagnostic certainty should not delay stabilization and monitoring.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old has suspected myocarditis. CMR demonstrates myocardial edema and patchy subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement. What is the best interpretation?

options.A: Findings support active/recent inflammatory myocardial injury
options.C: Findings are diagnostic of an atrial septal defect
options.D: Findings indicate isolated pericarditis without myocardial involvement

questions.rationale: Edema plus a nonischemic LGE pattern supports myocarditis and reflects myocardial injury/inflammation.

option_explanations.A: Correct. This is a characteristic CMR pattern.
option_explanations.B: Endocarditis is diagnosed by different clinical and imaging criteria.
option_explanations.C: ASD is a structural lesion and does not create this tissue pattern.
option_explanations.D: LGE within myocardium indicates myocardial involvement.
option_explanations.E: Scar/injury may be associated with arrhythmic risk rather than excluding it.

questions.board_pearl: CMR tissue findings add diagnostic confidence but must still be integrated with the clinical picture.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old with myocarditis is hypotensive with cool extremities and pulmonary edema. Which therapeutic principle best fits this hemodynamic state?

options.A: Prioritize therapies that improve perfusion while recognizing the risk of worsening congestion
options.B: Give unlimited crystalloid because all pediatric shock is volume depleted
options.C: Avoid vasoactive support because it can alter heart rate
options.E: Wait for biopsy before treating shock

questions.rationale: Cardiogenic shock requires restoration of perfusion with careful attention to preload and congestion; treatment should not be delayed for definitive etiologic testing.

option_explanations.A: Correct. This is the core hemodynamic principle.
option_explanations.B: Cardiogenic shock is not necessarily volume depleted and excessive fluid can be harmful.
option_explanations.D: Antipyretics do not address low output.
option_explanations.E: Shock treatment is immediate and independent of biopsy timing.

questions.board_pearl: Pediatric shock is not synonymous with fluid-responsive shock.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old with rapidly worsening myocarditis requires increasing vasoactive support and develops rising lactate and oliguria. The hospital has no pediatric mechanical circulatory support program. What is the best next step?

options.A: Continue local ward care until cardiac arrest occurs
options.B: Arrange urgent transfer to a center capable of advanced pediatric cardiac support
options.C: Send home with a wearable monitor
options.D: Wait several days to see if troponin falls

questions.rationale: Progressive low-output failure despite escalating support should trigger early transfer to a center capable of mechanical circulatory support and transplantation evaluation.

option_explanations.A: Delaying escalation risks irreversible organ injury.
option_explanations.B: Correct. Anticipatory transfer is a core management principle in severe pediatric myocarditis.
option_explanations.D: Troponin trends should not delay escalation.
option_explanations.E: Outpatient care is inappropriate in shock.

questions.board_pearl: Transfer before collapse when local resources cannot support the likely next step.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old with acute myocarditis asks whether recovery is guaranteed. Which response best reflects the expected clinical course?

options.A: All children recover completely within days
options.B: Outcomes range from full recovery to persistent dysfunction, mechanical support, transplantation, or death
options.C: Myocarditis always progresses to dilated cardiomyopathy
options.D: Normal blood pressure at presentation guarantees a benign course
options.E: Initial troponin alone determines long-term outcome

questions.rationale: Pediatric myocarditis has a broad trajectory, from complete recovery to severe heart failure and transplantation; early findings do not perfectly predict outcome.

option_explanations.B: Correct. This reflects the known variability.
option_explanations.C: Progression to DCM can occur but is not inevitable.
option_explanations.E: No single biomarker determines long-term outcome.

questions.board_pearl: Myocarditis is unpredictable enough that early clinical improvement should not erase follow-up needs.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old has unexplained tachycardia, gallop, hepatomegaly, and exercise intolerance. Which initial imaging test is most appropriate to assess ventricular function and structural cardiac disease?

options.B: Coronary CT angiography in every patient

questions.rationale: Echocardiography is the first-line imaging study in suspected pediatric myocarditis because it assesses ventricular function, chamber size, valves, pericardial effusion, thrombus, and structural alternatives.

option_explanations.A: Correct. It is fast, noninvasive, and directly assesses cardiac structure/function.
option_explanations.B: CT may be useful for specific coronary questions but is not first-line routinely.
option_explanations.C: Invasive catheterization is not the initial imaging test in most cases.
option_explanations.D: Does not adequately evaluate cardiac function.
option_explanations.E: Stress imaging is inappropriate during suspected active myocarditis.

questions.board_pearl: Echo first for function and structure; CMR later for tissue characterization when appropriate.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old athlete is several months out from myocarditis. Symptoms have resolved, troponin is normal, and LV systolic function has normalized. Which additional assessment is most relevant before competitive sports clearance?

options.A: Ambulatory rhythm monitoring and exercise testing as part of cardiology reassessment

questions.rationale: Return-to-play assessment includes evaluation for residual arrhythmia and functional recovery, not merely symptom and biomarker normalization.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Rhythm surveillance and exercise testing address exertional electrical risk.
option_explanations.E: Incomplete because arrhythmic risk can persist after symptom recovery.

questions.board_pearl: Sports clearance after myocarditis is a cardiac risk reassessment, not a symptom checklist.
